releases.title: Structured release notes
releases.summary: Release notes now live in one machine-readable file that ships inside coder, so a future update can show you what changed.

added.text: Release notes are kept in release-notes/releases.json, and CHANGELOG.md is generated from it.
added.details: coder carries its own copy of the notes. The updater does not show them yet.

releases.title: Multiple workspaces, SSH folders and slash commands mid-turn
releases.summary: Work across several local or SSH folders in one session, run slash commands while the agent is still working, and open a reminders pane.

added.text: Add more project folders to a session with /add <folder>. The agent's tools can work in all of them.
Add a folder on another machine with /add ssh <host>[:<path>].
added.details: Hosts come from ~/.ssh/config. Without a path you start in the remote home folder.

added.text: List workspaces with /dirs (or /workspaces), remove one with /dirs rm <name>, and pick the active one with /use <name>.
Typing /add shows hints as you type: a folder path or ssh <host>, your SSH hosts, and folder completion for local and connected remote folders.
When you have more than one workspace, the status bar shows the active one, like ⌂ name · 2.
The @ file picker also lists files in added local folders, as name:path.
Workspaces are saved with the session and come back when you resume it.
New /reminders pane lists your reminders and when each runs next.

changed.text: Slash commands typed while the agent is working now run instead of being sent to the agent as text.
changed.details: Most commands, such as /model, run right away and apply from the next request. /compact, /login, /logout, /update and changes to providers or MCP servers wait until the turn ends. /clear and Ctrl-L are refused until the turn ends.

changed.text: Running a pane command again closes that pane, and Esc closes an open side pane.
Side panes now get two thirds of the right column's height.

security.text: SSH passwords, key passphrases and one-time codes are asked for in the secure input card and are never saved or logged.
A new SSH host key needs your approval in a Yes/No card that defaults to No and is never answered automatically.
sudo on an SSH workspace uses the same approval card as local sudo.

notes: SSH support has been tested against a simulated ssh, not yet against a live server.
Remote login shells must be bash, zsh or sh. fish and csh are not supported.
Remote sudo asks for the password for each command unless the remote account has NOPASSWD set.
The @ file picker does not list files in SSH workspaces yet.

releases.title: Paste into question and secret cards
releases.summary: You can now paste into the agent's question cards and into password or token cards, safely.

added.text: Paste into question cards and secret (password or token) cards.

fixed.text: A pasted secret no longer keeps its trailing line break.
fixed.details: Line breaks pasted into a typed answer become spaces, so "one" and "two" on two lines reads "one two".

fixed.text: Very long pasted secrets show at most 32 dots and a character count, so the card stays on screen.

security.text: In terminals without bracketed paste, a line break inside a fast paste never submits a card.
security.details: A paste that starts in the first 0.3 seconds after a card appears is ignored with "paste ignored · try again", and leftover pasted text is not typed into the chat input.

security.text: The hidden buffer for a secret is wiped as it grows, so no stray copy stays in memory.

releases.title: Question cards are never answered for you
releases.summary: Questions and approvals from the agent always wait for your answer, and focus returns to an open card after menus.

security.text: The agent's questions are never answered automatically from a default.
security.details: When nobody can answer, such as in a headless run, the agent is told no answer is available, and approval questions count as not approved. A default only pre-selects a choice.

security.text: sudo and update prompts need an exact choice. An empty answer means no.

fixed.text: A card ignores keys other than Esc for 0.3 seconds after it appears, so text you were typing cannot answer it by accident.
Focus goes back to an open card after you close a menu, form or pane. Tab from the input reaches the card, and Ctrl-U clears the card's text.

releases.title: ergo by default, updates, reminders and a new look
releases.summary: Everything since 0.9.170: the ergo provider is the default, coder can update itself, and the TUI gained question cards, a file picker, reminders and refreshed colours.

added.text: ergo is now the default provider, ahead of local Ollama and Ollama Cloud. Sign in with /login, sign out with /logout, and check your wallet with /balance.
added.details: Sign-in uses a device code. Your token is kept in the system keychain or a private file. Running out of balance shows a clear message.

added.text: ergo models come in flash, pro and genius tiers, and the /model picker remembers your choice for each provider.
New Ollama Cloud provider, using OLLAMA_API_KEY.
coder checks for updates in the background. Install them with /update or coder update, or turn on automatic installs with coder update auto on.
The agent can ask you questions in a card in the transcript, and sudo commands need your approval first.
Attach files to a message with the @ file picker.
The reminder form has a schedule dropdown, date and time fields, a live preview of the schedule, and one-time reminders.
New coder reminders and coder tasks commands for the terminal.
Anonymous usage statistics and crash reports, controlled with /telemetry on, off or status.
The /compact hint shows which model compacts and how full its context window is.

changed.text: Colours follow your colour scheme, Markdown and code blocks render better, and the canvas uses the full height.

fixed.text: Provider selection and API version compatibility problems.
Slash commands and plain messages could freeze the UI.
Esc closes modal forms, and Ctrl-U deletes back to the start of the line.
/config keeps its Save and Cancel buttons visible, and the /about intro uses the normal pane width.
